cards.title: 3 Strategies for Supporting Kids' Mental Health Year-Round
cards.body: Parents and kids can establish healthy habits and routines that positively shape mental health. These strategies help get ahead of the school year's pile-up of stress.

cards.title: Helping Your Teen Survive Their First Heartbreak
cards.body: A teen's first breakup can be emotionally devastating and affect them for years. Parents can play a crucial role in helping their teen navigate this difficult time.

cards.title: When Motherhood Reactivates Unresolved Trauma
cards.body: Becoming a mother can awaken unresolved trauma, bringing old relational patterns and trauma triggers into the present. Understanding this connection helps mothers address these patterns.

cards.title: Back to School Teen Social Scene
cards.body: The start of a new school year requires social adjustment, and not all teens are wired the same. Parents can help by understanding their teen's social needs.

cards.title: Play Is Serious Business: Let Kids Have Fun!
cards.body: As schools have reduced recess, academic achievement has fallen and obesity has risen. Taking play seriously and letting kids have fun is crucial for child development.

cards.title: What Can I Do When My Child Rejects Me?
cards.body: Divorce can rupture family relationships and trust between parent and child. Healing can begin even when reconciliation hasn't started.

cards.title: Moving on and Final Advice for Parents Raising Kids
cards.body: This concluding installment of Once Upon a Child offers guidance for parents navigating their children's development. It provides final insights on parenting through life's stages.

cards.title: Why is the grass green and which was the deadliest dinosaur? The kids' quiz
cards.body: Five multiple-choice questions set by children test your knowledge. Submit your own junior brainteasers for future quizzes.

cards.title: The hill I will die on: A music festival isn't one without children
cards.body: Families can add magic to music festivals, and toddlers don't spoil the fun. The author braved festivals with her twins and discovered how kids enhance the experience.
